answers.rationale: Maya evaluates alternate airports by total savings, transfer burden, trip length, and arrival timing rather than applying a closest-airport rule. For a five-night car-based trip, SAV's substantially lower fare and earlier arrival can justify the additional drive; the rental-car plan is unchanged either way.

Carry-on-only fits this short solo itinerary and avoids unnecessary bag cost and handling, but Maya's history treats baggage as trip-specific rather than a universal rule. Add checked-bag timing only if bulky materials or other needs arise.

Six nights of ski gear, winter boots, a booster, and a likely oversized suitcase make one checked bag practical, especially when included. Airport planning should include bag-drop and baggage-claim time while essentials remain in carry-ons.

For a light three-night museum trip, carry-on-only is the efficient starting plan. A free checked bag should remain an option if gifts make it useful, at which point bag-drop and claim buffers need to be added rather than assumed from the outset.
